field_speed_re400: Retained Re=400 speed at h=1/32, with computed velocity streamlines. All four formulations are shown on the same physical color scale. Speed uses a linear color scale. These coarse-grid solutions are distinct from the selected fine-grid comparisons.
field_p_re400: Retained Re=400 zero-mean pressure at h=1/32, with computed velocity streamlines. All four formulations are shown on the same physical color scale. Signed fields use symmetric logarithmic normalization. These coarse-grid solutions are distinct from the selected fine-grid comparisons.
field_omega_re400: Retained Re=400 signed vorticity at h=1/32, with computed velocity streamlines. All four formulations are shown on the same physical color scale. Signed fields use symmetric logarithmic normalization. These coarse-grid solutions are distinct from the selected fine-grid comparisons.
convergence_re400: Retained Re=400, h=1/32 convergence. Upper: FV steady momentum defect. Lower: FD relative vorticity-update rate, divided by its time step. The equations, iteration units and stopping norms differ; their ordinate magnitudes cannot be used to rank formulation accuracy. Recorded costs are in the tables.

review_profiles_re400: Independent follow-up Re=400 velocity profiles for central convection. Solid lines use 32 FV cells per side; dashed lines use 64 where available. Black markers are Ghia samples. At Re=400 the red cross retains the isolated published anomaly without including it in the qualified norm. These fields and their timings belong to the separately identified follow-up suite.
review_coupling_re400: Independent follow-up Re=400, 32-cell central-convection histories against cumulative pressure solves. The dotted momentum line is the 1e-6 target. Divergence fluctuations near machine precision are not spatial error. Solve count is a work indicator, not an assertion that every linear solve has equal cost.

review_convection_re400: Independent follow-up Re=400 SIMPLE profiles: first-order upwind and central convection on the indicated meshes. Changing convection changes the spatial equations; this is separate from changing the pressure-velocity coupling algorithm. The isolated Ghia horizontal-profile anomaly is omitted from the qualified markers.
